observations: The product stops new membership/profile/delete/LDAP/signup writes to every old provider route.
Existing queued HTTP requests and background jobs are drained or cancelled without automatic replay.
Every old provider container/process and background worker has exited; IDs and exit observations are retained.
Restart policies, supervisors, old jobs and stale replicas cannot relaunch the unfenced binary.
For supported local SQLite the old process and its queues are gone. External/shared PostgreSQL is refused by this implementation; prior PostgreSQL protocol proof does not admit that topology.
The node executor observes these facts through its real runtime and storage boundary. Caller-supplied booleans are insufficient.
The supported existing-node lifecycle preserves the same data volume/database, encryption key, clients, users, groups and app data.
Only the qualified digest starts, and its genuine embedded migration 20261025060000 completes without a dirty migration state.
All serving replicas report the admitted digest and authenticated membership capability. No old/new rolling overlap is allowed.
A synthetic exactly bound local UUID acquires sticky required-CAS mode; the executor observes no-op advancement, stale rejection and missing-condition denial.
This occurs only after old writers are absent and before membership writes reopen.
Old browser forms and delayed requests are rejected or reloaded for explicit review; their stale selections are not automatically rebased.
Real installed Photos/Files journeys prove grant, revoke, restore, member leave and active-session behavior with synthetic test identities.
Final product readback proves the same node/stack/storage and preserves all existing apps/data.

failure_policy.missing_drain_or_executor_receipt: deny CAS activation and retain stopped admission; do not assert rollout success
failure_policy.failed_new_start_or_migration: halt and diagnose using the existing lifecycle; preserve storage and recovery evidence
failure_policy.managed_database_downgrade: refuse old/unfenced binaries; use a corrected forward release
failure_policy.restore: only the separately admitted existing recovery flow; no destructive or mixed-binary restoration is inferred
